title: Jonah and the Hollow
premise: Jonah Marchetti has spent his life drawing maps of realms he cannot enter, hiding his gift inside the valley where magic dies at the border stones. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive and burn the valley's records, Jonah learns his late mother sold his soul to the court beneath the mountain to buy his safe birth—and that the debt is now due. Fleeing into the unmapped wilds with a disgraced huntress named Wren, he discovers his cartography is itself a magic: what he draws, he can walk. To reclaim his soul before winter seals the mountain, Jonah must out-bargain a hollow king who feeds on memory, sacrificing pieces of his own past to survive the ascent—until he chooses to give up the memory of Wren rather than let the crown weaponize his gift, ending the story with him whole but unremembering, mapping a world he no longer knows he saved.
about_author: Ada Vasquez is a former surveyor who spent six years charting river basins before turning to fiction, and her maps still hang in three provincial archives. She writes fantasy about people who measure the world and are measured by it in return.

chapters.title: The Border Stones
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He finishes a map of a realm he'll never see, trading sketches for bread in a valley where magic cannot cross the border stones. When a crown proclamation arrives naming gifted folk as traitors, his neighbor is taken in the night. The emotional beat: quiet dread—the safety he built is revealed as borrowed time.

chapters.title: What Mother Signed
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Ransacking his mother's effects, Jonah finds a contract bearing his own name: his soul, sold to the court beneath the mountain before his birth. A huntress, Wren, catches him burning the papers—but she's deserted the hunt rather than kill children. Beat: grief curdling into resolve; he must leave the valley.

chapters.title: Ink That Walks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Crossing the border stones, they expect Jonah's gift to die; instead his sketch of the pass becomes a real path where none existed. Wren realizes the crown wants him not dead but harvested. Beat: wonder shadowed by fear—his survival tool is exactly what makes him prey.

chapters.title: The Toll Road
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They reach a market town where memories are traded as currency, and Jonah pays for lodging with the recollection of his mother's face. Wren warns him the hollow court buys through such places. Beat: first taste of the price of survival—he feels lighter and less himself.

chapters.title: Hunters in the Snow
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Her former captain corners them; Wren kills him to save Jonah and can no longer go home. Jonah secretly maps an escape route so detailed it exhausts him for days. Beat: guilt and intimacy deepen—they are each other's only witnesses now.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They descend into the mountain city, where the hollow king rules over shelves of bottled souls. Jonah finds his own jar, warm and beating like a heart. The king offers a trade: the soul for Jonah's service as royal mapmaker. Beat: temptation—power offered freely, corruption dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Drawn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Jonah accepts, redrawing the kingdom's borders overnight and erasing three rebel villages from existence. Wren confronts him; he no longer remembers why the villages mattered—or fully why she does. Beat: horror at how easily power rewrites a man.

chapters.title: The Empty Shelf
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A fragment of forgotten self—a sketch of Wren hidden in his boot—cracks the king's hold. He learns the king is hollow because he once sold his own soul upward, to something older beneath the mountain. Beat: clarity through loss; the chain of debts has a bottom.

chapters.title: Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Jonah and Wren's alternating POV. As the long winter seals the passes, Jonah shatters the soul-shelves, freeing hundreds of memories that flood back to their scattered owners—including the king's, which unmakes him mid-sentence. Beat: climax—sacrifice, chaos, and the collapse of the court.

chapters.title: Cartographer of Nothing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Whole again but stripped of every memory bought and bargained, Jonah wakes in spring beside a woman he doesn't recognize holding maps in his own hand. He begins drawing the world anew, starting with her face. Beat: bittersweet resolution—memory lost, but a self worth remapping remains.
